title: Microburst deploy docket and release digest 2026-04-11
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is the working docket for the Microburst (v2) release targeting a phased lane rollout for inference-serving surface area. It combines the condensed hour-by-hour watch roster, preflight checklist, rollout calendar, and a draft of the public release notes we can iterate on. Meant to be a small-batch, low-latency focused release: feature set is request batching heuristics + a KV-cache eviction tweak.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Ship batching heuristic change (optimize small, frequent requests) with minimal tail latency impact.
- Validate KV-cache eviction improvement under sustained long-context traces.
- Keep customer-facing latency SLOs stable; no more than +5% 99th on p99 token latency during canary.
- Collect quality signals (LLM output diffs) on a set of golden prompts.

Key risks and mitigations (notes):
- Risk: sudden p99 regressions from batching corner cases. Mitigation: canary at 5% traffic with throttled burst and auto-fallback to prior policy.
- Risk: cache churn causing memory spikes. Mitigation: memory soft limit alarms + auto-eviction heuristics pinned at conservative defaults for first 24h.
- Risk: rollout config mis-applied across regions. Mitigation: region-tagged rollout pins and preflight dry-run (see preflight step 4).

Rollout calendar (phased):
- Day -2 (2026-04-09): Finalize release artifact build. Confirm infra images, publish build hash (runtime:v2-microburst-20260409). Smoke-run in sandbox.
- Day -1 (2026-04-10): Staging cutover and rolling smoke tests. Post SMOKE board signoff by SRE and QA. Queue canary.
- Day 0 (2026-04-11) Canary start 09:00UTC: route 1% traffic region-na, 30m ramp to 5% if no p99 regressions.
  - 09:30UTC: telemetry snapshot and call (ops-channel).
  - 12:00UTC: decision gate: hold / proceed to 20% / rollback. Decision criteria spelled below.
- Day 0 (2026-04-11) Canary expand 12:30UTC: If green, 5% -> 20% over 45m; add eu-west as secondary canary region at 2.5%.
- Day 0 (2026-04-11) 18:00UTC: If still green, push to 50% and enable conservative fallback policy for heavy-tail requests.
- Day 1 (2026-04-12) 10:00UTC: Ramp to 100% for non-enterprise (hosted) region pools; enterprise/dedicated remain opt-in for 72h.

Decision gate metrics (pass/fail heuristics):
- Latency: p99 token latency <= baseline_p99 * 1.05 AND p50 within +/-10%.
- Errors: 5xx rate does not exceed baseline by >0.1% absolute.
- Resource: memory usage per-worker < baseline + 10% and no OOMs observed.
- Quality: golden-prompt delta score (BLEU-like / custom similarity) does not exceed threshold; see linked artifact for eval harness.
- Customer impact: no open escalations from CS during window.

Preflight checklist (assign owner):
- Build and artifact: verify image hash and tag (owner: Ben).
- Canary config: YAML validation + region pins (owner: Claire).
- Telemetry dashboards: instantiate temporary snapshot dashboard (owner: Diego).
- Smoke tests: generate 10k synthetic requests across context-length distribution (owner: QA lead) — include golden prompt sampling.
- Rollback plan: validate previous release route and quick switch keys (owner: SRE on-call).
- KMS / Secrets: confirm keys available in eu/na (owner: security infra).
- Stakeholder comms: schedule 09:30UTC ops call and 12:00UTC decision thread (owner: release lead — Aisha).
- Cost guardrails: set token budget alarms for the first 48h (owner: finance-ops).
- Customer knobs: ensure dedicated customers are excluded by policy unless explicitly opted in (owner: account-provisioning).

Operator playbook (hour-by-hour condensed):
- T-30m: ensure release artifact present in registry; confirm canary route is staged and paused. Quick sanity: run 100 synthetic requests.
- T-0: open ops-call, unpause canary. Monitor p50/p90/p99, 5xx, worker mem, token spend.
- T+15m: short telemetry note in the release thread — attach first snapshot.
- T+30m: evaluate for regressions; if any soft anomalies (p99 +3–4% but stable), hold and move to extended 60m observation.
- T+60m: decision point: continue expand / hold / rollback. If rollback: unroute canary and scale down new pools.
- T+6h: mid-day digest (ops-call optional): annotate root-cause if any anomalies.
- T+24h: finalize 24h telemetry and start post-release retro notes.

Telemetry and observability (quick refs):
- Dashboards: microburst-eval (p50/p90/p99 by region, errors, mem), golden-prompts-diff.
- Logs: enable sample-level verbose for 5% of requests in canary. Tag logs with release=microburst.
- Traces: trace slow tokens and sample traces where KV-cache eviction occurred.
- Alerts: temp alert suppression for non-critical noisy rules; do not suppress memory OOM / 5xx higher-severity.

Comms templates (ops channel and external):
- Ops-channel post (short): "Starting Microburst canary 09:00UTC region-na -> 1% -> 5% over 30m. Owners: Aisha (release), Ben (build), Claire (routing), Diego (telemetry). Decision gate @12:00UTC."
- Customer-facing blurb (draft): "We’re rolling a small performance improvement to request batching that reduces cost for short-context requests while preserving latency. No action required. We’ll notify if any impact is detected."

Rollback decision rubric (short):
- Immediate rollback triggers: sustained p99 > baseline * 1.10 OR error-rate spike > +0.5% absolute OR any customer escalation marked P0.
- Soft rollback (throttle back): p99 between 1.05–1.10 for >30m AND resource trending up. Throttle canary to 1% and investigate.

Post-release notes (internal draft — will be refined for external release notes):
- Release name: Microburst v2
- Release date: 2026-04-11
- Summary: Small-batch rollout of batching heuristic changes and a KV-cache eviction policy update. Objective: improve throughput for short queries and reduce per-token cost without degrading tail latency.
- What changed: batching algorithm now prefers short-window bundling for requests <150 tokens; KV-cache eviction switches from LRU->size-aware-LRU with a 2-tier aging window.
- Why: customers saw inefficient batching for low-latency short requests on hosted API; early bench shows 8–12% token-cost reduction in synthetic workloads.
- Known limitations: heavy long-context workloads may see slightly higher cache churn during learning window; enterprise pools remain opt-in for 72h.
- Rollout plan: phased canary -> regional expansion -> full non-enterprise rollout.
- How to revert: runtime route switch to runtime:v2-microburst-legacy or previous runtime tag (ops playbook has exact commands).
- Monitoring checklist: p50/p90/p99, 5xx, mem, golden-prompt diffs, token spend.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- QA: confirm golden-prompt diff thresholds (exact numeric bound) with model-evals team — Claire to chase.
- Observability: add a targeted histogram for batch sizes by request type. Diego owns instrumentation rollout.
- Enterprise communication: draft SR for managed customers who might opt-in early. Aisha to coordinate with solutions-eng.
- Post-release retro: schedule 2h slot 2026-04-13 11:00UTC.

Quick appendices / run snippets (ops cheats):
- Canary route (k8s-ish): kubectl apply -f canary-route-microburst.yaml --namespace=prod
- Quick rollback: kubectl set image deployment/runtime runtime=runtime:v2-stable --namespace=prod
- Snapshot command: /ops/telemetry/snapshot --dashboard microburst-eval --window 00:30

Draft external release note (short):
- Headline: Microburst v2: smarter batching for short requests and cost savings
- Body: Today we deployed Microburst v2, which refines request batching behavior to better group short, frequent requests and updates our cache eviction policy to be more size-aware. Early internal tests show lower per-token costs for interactive short queries with no meaningful latency regressions. We’ll continue monitoring performance across regions and will share details in the release changelog.

End of docket.
If anything else needs to be dropped in here (customer links, PR links), add to linked_artifacts and ping on #release-ops.

---
Notes: this is intentionally compact and somewhat informal — transfer to Confluence after post-release retro if we want a long-term canonical page.

Change log of this doc: 2026-04-11 initial draft by Aisha; 2026-04-12 added telemetry owners and decision thresholds (Ben/Diego); 2026-04-13 clarified rollback rubric and scheduled retro.
